problem:
Determine if the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 5\end{aligned}]$ 
is diagonalizable or not, and if it is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Whether a Given 2x2 Matrix Is Diagonalizable
examples.problem:
Determine if the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069391/assets/dfc9ee546f72ad68cf116b8f67d165ba9b6ff6e77dce88f145dda93f13091441.png)
is diagonalizable or not, and if it is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
examples.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is triangular, the eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal. 

So, the eigenvalues are $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=3.$ Since we get one repeated eigenvalue, the matrix might not be diagonalizable. To check this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-3I\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -5 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has only $1$ pivot column. This implies that we will have only $2-1=1$ linearly independent eigenvector corresponding to the current eigenvalue. Therefore, $A$ is not diagonalizable.

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ c & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ c & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-2,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}.
$$

 

In conclusion, we get $a=-2,$ $b=3,$ and $c=-2.$
